user: And what are the typical timelines?
answer:
The knowledge base sets these review timelines:

- **Card reason codes:** a review target of 10 business days.
- **Transfer reason codes:** a review target of 20 business days.
- **Complex cases with a foreign acquirer:** up to 45 calendar days. You are notified if your case falls into this category.

The documentation doesn't say whether `service_not_rendered` counts as a card or a transfer reason code, so I can't confirm which of the first two timelines applies to your dispute. Your dispute was opened under that code, so a human agent can confirm the exact timeline for your case. Would you like me to escalate it?

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each dispute reason code has its own window, counted in days from the
transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).

Glossary
## Provisional credit
A temporary refund applied while a dispute is reviewed; reversed if the dispute
is declined.
